video.title: SpaceX Lowers IPO Valuation Target | Bloomberg Tech 5/29/2026

thesis: A week of record AI-driven valuations — SpaceX trimming its IPO target to $1.8T, Anthropic eclipsing OpenAI at $965B, Dell's blowout server guide — tests whether investors are paying for present fundamentals or a decade-out dream, with Blue Origin's exploded rocket as a reminder the dream isn't guaranteed.

chapters.title: Benedikt Kammel — SpaceX IPO valuation cut
Silas Brown — Anthropic's $36B private credit deal
David Kennedy, Dell — AI server blowout
Janet Mui, RBC Brewin Dolphin — build to deployment
Matthew Weir, Goldman — AI productivity & jobs
Carolina Parada, Google DeepMind — embodied AI
Loren Grush — Blue Origin New Glenn explosion

insights.headline: SpaceX IPO target trimmed $2T to $1.8T
insights.body: Sources say SpaceX is now targeting a $1.8 trillion valuation, down from the >$2 trillion Bloomberg reported in April. Editor Benedikt Kammel frames the cut as positioning — 'a rounding error' at this scale — and notes Musk publicly replied 'false' to the report.

insights.headline: SpaceX implies a 96x price-to-sales multiple
insights.body: With $18.7B in 2025 revenue (up from $14B in 2024), a $1.8T valuation is roughly 96x sales — versus ~10x for typical software companies. Buyers are paying for the opportunity (a stated $28T TAM, a million people on Mars), not current fundamentals.

insights.headline: SpaceX sum-of-the-parts: XAI + comms + launch
insights.body: Bloomberg Intelligence's George Ferguson breaks the ~$2T into pieces: ~$400B for XAI (Mandeep's team), ~$600B for the satellite constellation (John Butler), and a launch business valued at ~90x revenue (Rocket Lab comp) worth roughly $1.2T including internal launches not in reported revenue.

insights.headline: Anthropic passes OpenAI at $965B valuation
insights.body: Anthropic closed a round at a $965B valuation ($900B pre-money), surpassing OpenAI (last ~$700B+ pre-money) for the first time. Nearing $50B run-rate revenue, it roughly doubled revenue in months — three years after having essentially no product to sell.

insights.headline: A $30B round ballooned to $65B in weeks
insights.body: Rebecca Torrence reports Anthropic's round originally targeted ~$30B but closed at $65B amid excess demand, with strategic commitments from hyperscalers Google and Amazon plus four VC leads. The fundraise does not change Anthropic's IPO timeline — it could still go public as soon as this fall.

insights.headline: AI debt is private credit's escape from SaaS
insights.body: Silas Brown explains Apollo and Blackstone are syndicating a ~$36B debt deal for Anthropic's infrastructure. The irony: private credit funds over-concentrated in software-as-a-service are now parking insurance capital in the very AI 'disrupting the SaaS industry' — pivoting to investment-grade AI and energy-transition lending.

insights.headline: Dell's best day ever on $60B AI server guide
insights.body: Dell lifted full-year sales guidance to $167B (up $27B), with AI server guide raised $10B to $60B and EPS of $17.90. CFO David Kennedy stressed growth is 'broad-based' — traditional server/networking grew 92% in Q1 — not one hyperscaler. Shares jumped 30%+, the S&P 500's top performer.

insights.headline: AI is shifting from build phase to deployment
insights.body: RBC's Janet Mui argues the AI trade is broadening from infrastructure build-out to enterprise deployment. She flags memory as a two-year-plus bottleneck (Micron passed a $1T market cap) and warns that if every firm adopts AI without a competitive moat, the surplus flows to consumers, not corporate profits.

insights.headline: Goldman sees AI lifting US trend GDP to 2.4%
insights.body: Goldman's Matthew Weir says ~25% of US economic tasks could be automated gradually over a decade, freeing workers for higher-productivity roles and raising trend real GDP growth to 2.4%. He cites MIT work showing most of today's 170M US occupations didn't exist in 1940.

insights.headline: Only chipmakers actually profit from AI today
insights.body: Weir warns the AI flywheel only self-perpetuates if enterprise users generate profits from their AI spend. Right now funding comes from external investors and hyperscaler cash flow, and 'the only part of the stack generating a lot of profits' is the semiconductor companies — a key vulnerability for private valuations.

insights.headline: Muddy Waters: 15% of knowledge workers displaced
insights.body: Muddy Waters CEO Carson Block's house view is 15% net displacement of knowledge workers, possibly within single-digit years and as soon as three, because AI capability is improving faster than humans can adapt — a sharply more bearish take than Goldman's.

insights.headline: Robotics' real edge is human-world nuance
insights.body: Google DeepMind's Carolina Parada says much of what looks impressive in robotics is 'predefined, memorized sequences.' The hard, defensible problem is genuine intelligence to handle unstructured, changing human environments and dexterous tasks like folding origami or packing a lunchbox — what Gemini Robotics (going into Boston Dynamics' Atlas) is pushing on.

insights.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn explodes on the pad
insights.body: Loren Grush reports New Glenn exploded in a massive fireball during a hot-fire test, with no injuries and Amazon Leo satellites not aboard. It jeopardizes a $10B contract backlog and Blue Origin's NASA Artemis lunar lander role — though NASA deliberately also funds SpaceX as a backup lander.

insights.headline: SpaceX IPO could be the biggest ever at $75B
insights.body: A Bloomberg Originals segment notes SpaceX's IPO is expected to raise as much as $75B — more than double Saudi Aramco's record $29.4B in 2019 — making it the largest IPO of all time. The XAI merger and capital needs reversed Musk's earlier reluctance to go public.

action_items: Stress-test any AI valuation against profits, not promise: ask whether enterprise users are actually generating returns on their AI spend, because today only chipmakers are clearly profitable.
When chasing AI beneficiaries outside tech, favor firms with a real moat and capital to spend — undifferentiated adopters will see AI surplus competed away to consumers.
Treat memory/DRAM as a multi-year bottleneck (and investable theme) rather than a passing shortage, per executives quoted across the AI hardware chain.
Read mega-cap private valuations (SpaceX ~96x sales) as bets on a 5–20 year dream; size positions to the chance the dream slips, as Blue Origin's explosion illustrates.
